decisions.question: The operator has neither Entra app-registration rights nor Azure RBAC role-assignment rights, so neither the desktop-to-support-API leg nor the support-API-to-Foundry managed-identity leg can be provisioned. How does anything reach the real Foundry project?
decisions.decision: Add a development-gated Foundry credential that reads an API key from an environment variable, and run the support API locally in Development composition. Swap only the credential mechanism; keep the entire architecture. Deployment discovery, the profile registry, the effective catalog, route resolution, the Responses adapter, output validation, and signed receipts all stay exactly as designed.
decisions.notInManifest: This is an addition to the 36-task plan, made necessary by a real environment constraint. It does not replace FND-021; the managed-identity path is still built and remains the only production path.
invariantsThatMustHold: Production composition must refuse the development credential, proved by a test, using the same fail-closed guard shape the fake Foundry server already uses for Development and Test only.
FND-065's acceptance criterion survives unchanged: there is still no production API-key path. The development credential is structurally unreachable outside Development and Test.
The API key is read from an environment variable, never committed, never logged, never placed in telemetry, a problem document, or a receipt.
The credential-binding hash must incorporate the credential mechanism, so a receipt produced under the development credential can never be mistaken for one produced under managed identity.

openRisk.summary: The Foundry project deployments API may require an Entra token and may not accept an API key at all. API-key auth is generally available on the OpenAI-compatible inference surface, not necessarily on the project management surface.
openRisk.ifDiscoveryRejectsTheKey: Fall back to an operator-declared deployment inventory file, loaded only in Development, clearly labelled untrusted, and fed into the same normalizer and catalog cache. This preserves the architecture: the catalog is still built from an inventory, it is simply a declared one rather than a discovered one.
openRisk.cheapTest: Call the deployments URL with an api-key header instead of a bearer token and record the status class.

consequences: FND-002 can never reach ready=true in this environment, because identity attachment and role assignment are unobtainable, not merely unsupplied.
FND-064 and FND-065 remain blocked. The deployed posture requires Entra and RBAC regardless of this extension.
The desktop-to-support-API leg still needs an app registration for production. Locally it uses the existing development authentication adapters.

decisions.question: Who runs the Azure-facing verification steps?
decisions.decision: This development machine has no Azure connectivity and never will. Every Azure-facing step is executed by the operator on a separate work machine. No task may plan to run az, deploy a template, or call the Foundry project from this repository's development environment.
consequences: FND-002 stays permanently blocked in this environment. It can only reach ready=true from an operator run elsewhere.

Every Azure-facing tool must be a self-contained, operator-runnable script that validates its own inputs, refuses to persist secrets, and emits a redacted report the operator can hand back without leaking tenant data.
The deliverable for FND-002, FND-060, FND-061, FND-062, and FND-064 is a script plus a runbook, not an executed run.
Local gates must remain fully provable offline against the deterministic fake, because that is the only evidence this environment can generate.
decisions.handbackProtocol: The prerequisite and smoke reports are redacted by construction, so the operator can paste them back verbatim. They carry counts, status classes, hashes, and blocker codes, never endpoints, tokens, deployment names, or response bodies.

decisions.question: How do normalized model stream events reach the renderer, given that streaming does not exist anywhere in Rust or TypeScript today?
decisions.decision: Follow the plan exactly. Expose one separately fixed, reviewed support route and encode it in the generated contracts and in SupportStageRoute; never accept a renderer-provided URL. Publish normalized stream events to the renderer through a reviewed host surface and update the Tauri capability allowlist with a machine-readable minimum-capability test, exactly as FND-044 requires.
decisions.rejectedAlternative: Overloading the existing host_projection_events channel would have avoided any capability change, but the plan requires the streaming surface to be encoded in the generated contracts and the reviewed route allowlist.
consequences: reqwest needs its stream feature enabled in the workspace dependency.
FND-044 must add the capability allowlist entry and the minimum-capability test; no generic HTTP, path, shell, or secret command may be added alongside it.
Rust never parses raw Foundry SSE. The support API normalizes first and Rust decodes only generated ModelStreamEvent values.

planDivergences.planSays: Create runtime validators using generated contract validation.
planDivergences.repositoryIs: apps/desktop-ui does not depend on @sapphirus/contracts at all. Every wire type is hand-written in src/lib/hostClient/contracts.ts and re-validated in validation.ts. The map records this as deliberate defence in depth: the renderer re-validates the host's replies rather than trusting a shared type.
planDivergences.resolution: Keep the repository's pattern. Hand-write the catalog validators against the canonical schema rather than importing generated types into the renderer.

planDivergences.planSays: Normalize streaming events end to end.
planDivergences.repositoryIs: There is no streaming anywhere in Rust or TypeScript today. host_dispatch is request/response, the renderer CSP allows only ipc:, and reqwest is pinned without the stream feature.
planDivergences.resolution: Streaming is net-new transport, not a normalization of something existing. It must ride the existing projection-event channel or a new reviewed Tauri surface, and reqwest needs its stream feature.
